title: Evals offline fixture
description: The scripted socket an offline run replays. It is keyed by cell id, so a cell's answers cannot depend on how many cells ran before it, and it is deliberately explicit about what it does not say: a cell with no entry is not 'no answer', it is a fixture that cannot run that cell, and the runner reports it rather than inventing a refusal. The scripts use the production offline adapter's own vocabulary (text, provider failure, truncated stream, HTTP status plus body), so a fixture cannot express an outcome the adapter could not produce.

description.description: What this fixture is meant to demonstrate. It is read by a person, never by the runner.

cells.description: Scripted answers per cell id. A chat cell lists its stream scripts in order; a decision cell lists its HTTP responses in order. Running past the end is an error rather than a repeat of the last answer, so a fixture cannot hide a repair loop that never terminated.

usagePayload.description: A provider usage payload, exactly as a provider would send it. Kept opaque on purpose: the shape belongs to the provider, and the mapping that reads it is the shared one.

chatScript.description: One scripted chat stream. text arrives and the production parser reads it; failure is the provider declaring its own failure; truncated is a stream that ends with no terminal finish, as a dropped connection does.

response.description: One scripted HTTP response. The body is a string so a non-JSON body, the case a real endpoint returns under stress, is expressible.
